title: One week since my first Steam Coming Soon page — here's the honest feedback I got and what I did with it
author: PairOfPixelsGS
selftext:
One week in since dropping the first trailer and Coming Soon page for SLAMTOWN, my solo beat 'em up project. Wanted to share what the first week of community feedback actually looked like for me.

The reception was honestly better than I expected for a first trailer from a solo dev with no audience. People responded warmly to the concept, the co-op mechanic and art/graphics specifically, and that positive reaction gave me the motivation to take the critical feedback seriously rather than get discouraged by it.

And the critical feedback was brutally honest and exactly what I needed. Main themes that came up:

* Game felt too slow paced — movement and hits both
* Too floaty, low gravity
* Hard to distinguish players from enemies and foreground from background
* Hit impact not feeling impactful enough, especially in the air
* Combo names were too generic
* Enemy health bars misaligned / not positioned correctly

I went through everything and categorized it in a Google Sheets document. Some things I fixed immediately — combo names and health bar alignment are done. The bigger ones (pacing, gravity, hit impact, visual contrast) are actively being worked on and need proper validation before I call them fixed.

The lore not being clear in the trailer and character model fluidity are still on the list — those need more thought before I touch them.

Honestly the most valuable part wasn't any single piece of feedback — it was seeing the same issues flagged independently by multiple people. When five different people say "too floaty" without talking to each other, you stop second-guessing whether it's a real problem.

Still a long way to go — no demo yet, targeting 2-3 months. But this first week taught me more than the previous month of solo development before launching the page.

Happy to answer anything about the process.

comments.author: Juzzaman
comments.body:
I'm surprised this got attention tbh, it looks like an arcade game from the 90s to me. But is that the style and what people liked?

How much of the process is done by A.I tools?

replies.author: PairOfPixelsGS
replies.body:
Hi! This genre generally favors on old styles. My inspiration was Street Fighter 4 models, and that was the starting point for the characters. I think the feedback was good because people can relate it to other games, in a positive way. Another reason is that most old arcade games were pixel art made, and even the new remakes are also being done with it, so I wanted to do it a bit different, and that brings some "fresh air" to the genre, as the game is 2.5D with 3D characters in orthographic projection, and I also added some celshading to it, so I think that all of that together brought a positive reaction. For the AI tools, it was basically Midjourney -> Magnific ->  Gemini -> Meshy. I posted a part of the process here, if you are interested.  
[Solo dev here — I used AI to design characters for my beat 'em up game SLAMTOWN. Here's the full process behind enemy #2 (Enforcer) : r/aigamedev](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1u34ggg/solo_dev_here_i_used_ai_to_design_characters_for/)

comments.author: Old_Ktulu
comments.body: Will you answer questions with AI the same way you made this post?

replies.author: PairOfPixelsGS
replies.body: Hi! No, the post being the first cold contact with the community could need some assistance in writing, reviewing, and summarize the content in a good way. The comments are much more directional and objective, usually creating the connection with the commenter, so I don't really need AI for that. (Hope you don't think this was also AI generated)

comments.author: BenTheSodaman
comments.body:
Olá, PairOfPixelsGS,

Se você se sentir mais à vontade em português, eu diria para postar em português no futuro. Por algum motivo, as pessoas por aqui parecem perder a cabeça quando alguém usa IA para traduzir as postagens. 

Eu sei que não existem muitos lugares na internet para falar sobre IA gamedev, e é bem chato que você tenha recebido esse tipo de reação ao compartilhar.

replies.author: PairOfPixelsGS
replies.body: I appreciate your concern, and thanks a lot for the support. People can agree or disagree, have their own opinions, and that is fine. The goal here is always to help
